judged_text: The `updateEvent` fallback branch computes `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` inside a branch where `externalCalendarId` is falsy (null/empty), so the find predicate can never match and the expression is always undefined. Updating a legacy booking whose calendar reference has no externalCalendarId now passes `calendarId: undefined` to the Google API instead of the destination calendar's externalId, failing every reschedule/edit for bookings whose reference lacks the external ID.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent()`, the fallback was changed from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` (and similarly in `deleteEvent`). But this expression is evaluated specifically when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (because the ternary’s else-branch runs), so it searches for a calendar whose `externalId` equals a falsy value, which will not match normal destination calendars. That makes `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` end up `undefined` (or wrong), whereas previously it would use the destination calendar externalId. This is a diff-verifiable regression for legacy references lacking `externalCalendarId`.
